fit: oral dietary corn oil and rat salivary flow
assessment: Corn oil was the base diet. After 30 days, cannulated submandibular flow was lower in the retained corn arm than in the chia replacement arm. The experiment measures secretion in healthy rats and does not measure clinical drooling.

fit: shared oral Parkinson trial carrier and UPDRS part II total
assessment: The treatment table provides an overall part II score. Salivation item changes are unavailable and all arms used corn oil.

fit: oral Parkinson trial corn vehicle and seated cardiovascular monitoring
assessment: The trial measured seated wrist blood pressure and found no significant contrast. Standing changes and symptoms were not measured as an endpoint.

fit: Parkinson CBD trial dizziness reporting with oral corn vehicle
assessment: The associated thesis reports dizziness in the active arm. Posture and an oil-specific comparison are unavailable.

fit: self-reported cooking corn oil and seated blood pressure
assessment: Predominant corn-oil users had lower seated pressure than people mainly using animal fats. Self-reported exposure, seated monitoring and absence of a symptom endpoint limit the finding.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and sustained-attention task
assessment: No clear performance difference emerged against two DHA doses in healthy children. Neuroimaging and fatty acid correlations do not estimate an oil-induced change in attention in Parkinson disease.

fit: oral Parkinson trial vehicle and aggregate cognition
assessment: All arms had corn oil and the aggregate cognition endpoint offers no attention task or attention-specific item result.

fit: measured mouse stride with matched corn oil vehicle
assessment: Exposure group comparisons estimate PCB effects on matched oil backgrounds. The most shortened strides were in PCB-treated wild-type animals.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and timed mobility
assessment: Timed Up and Go was slower at follow-up in the corn arm and faster in the fish arm. The task combines several components and no stride lengths were reported.

fit: shared Parkinson trial vehicle and aggregate mobility
assessment: The mobility score does not give stride length, and both CBD arms also used corn oil.

fit: oral Parkinson trial vehicle and communication domain
assessment: The placebo group communication change was zero and groups were not clearly different. No speech intelligibility measure is available, and oil exposure was shared.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and functional mobility
assessment: Timed Up and Go differences concern task performance. Incidence or frequency of daily-life falls was not measured.

fit: mouse beam slips and matched corn oil vehicle
assessment: The relative number of slips varied by genotype with PCB exposure. Both arms used corn oil and beam slips differ from daily-life falls.

fit: Parkinson corn-vehicle study and aggregate mobility
assessment: The treatment table provides no item-level fall result or prospective counts, and the carrier was shared across randomized groups.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and prespecified fatigue ratings
assessment: A Japanese registry identifies a completed healthy-adult study measuring fatigue around mental work and on awakening. The record has no arm-level results or refining grade.

fit: injected corn oil vehicle and measured mouse olfaction
assessment: The control and toxin groups had matched injected corn oil. Olfactory differences reflect toxin or training contrasts on a shared vehicle background.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and apathy item in Alzheimer disease
assessment: Among item-positive patients, average apathy was higher after six months in the corn group. The comparative estimate was inconclusive and enrollment was for Alzheimer disease.

fit: shared oral Parkinson trial corn vehicle and part I aggregate
assessment: The treatment table gives no motivation item change or independent contrast for oil.
